back: A program being executed, with the resources it is using.
Running several processes at the same time by sharing the processor between them.
Running (using the processor), ready (waiting for the processor), blocked (waiting for an event such as input or output).
Ready to running (scheduled); running to ready (time slice ends); running to blocked (waits for I/O); blocked to ready (I/O completes).
Turnaround = completion - arrival. Waiting = turnaround - burst.
Each process runs for a fixed time slice, then goes to the back of the ready queue; pre-emptive and fair.
SJF: shortest burst runs next, no pre-emption. SRT: pre-empts when a process with a shorter remaining time arrives.
Runs in order of arrival; simple but a long job at the front delays the rest.
Saves the running process's registers, runs the scheduler and loads the next process's registers (a context switch).
